title: Canonical ordinary proper/open adjunction mate
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and, for a scheme $X$, let $D_\Lambda(X)=D(\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda))$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use inverse image $f^*$ [def-sfb-finite-upper-star], direct image $f_*$ [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], and exact open extension $j_!$ [sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek]. Put $P_f=Lf^*$ and $R_f=Rf_*$, with the canonical derived adjunction $P_f\dashv R_f$ [sk-def-sfb-finite-derived-functors]. Identify $P_f$ with termwise inverse image by [def-sfb-finite-derived-pullback-iso]. Transport the open adjunction of [def-sfb-finite-derived-extension-by-zero-adjunction] across that identification to obtain $J_j\dashv P_j$, where $J_j=D(j_!)$. For composable opens $j:U\to V$, $k:V\to X$, the open-extension compositor $J_kJ_j\cong J_{k\circ j}$ is the unique-left-adjoint comparison determined by these adjunctions and the derived inverse-image compositor induced by [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp]; equality transport of open maps is defined in the same way. For a clopen immersion $s$, define $\pi_s:1\to J_sP_s$ by the unit of $P_s\dashv R_s$ followed by the canonical identification $R_s\cong J_s$ (exact direct image for a clopen immersion); this is the identity on the image of $s$ and zero on its open complement. Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}A&\xrightarrow{k}&B\\r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\C&\xrightarrow{i}&D\end{array}$$
be a commutative square with $k,i$ quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] and $r,p$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]; write $h:p\circ k=i\circ r$. Form $B_C=B\times_D C$ with projections $b:B_C\to B$, $q:B_C\to C$, and its canonical clopen lift $t=(k,r):A\to B_C$ as in [def-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-arrows]. Use the ordinary constant-coefficient open base-change isomorphism $\beta:P_pJ_i\xrightarrow{\sim}J_bP_q$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change], transported to total derived pullbacks. Define
$$\alpha:P_pJ_i\xrightarrow{\beta}J_bP_q\xrightarrow{J_b\pi_tP_q}J_bJ_tP_tP_q\xrightarrow{\sim}J_kP_r,$$
where the last isomorphism uses $bt=k$, $qt=r$ and the specified open-extension and inverse-image compositors. Define the proper/open mate $\gamma:J_iR_r\to R_pJ_k$ to be the adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of this $\alpha$ under $P_r\dashv R_r$ and $P_p\dashv R_p$: explicitly
$$J_iR_r\xrightarrow{\eta_p}R_pP_pJ_iR_r\xrightarrow{R_p\alpha R_r}R_pJ_kP_rR_r\xrightarrow{R_pJ_k\varepsilon_r}R_pJ_k.$$
These definitions specify the actual ordinary-site comparison; they assert no tensor-compatibility or invertibility theorem.

lean.statement:
def properOpenMate (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {A B C D : Scheme.{u}} (k : A ⟶ B) (r : A ⟶ C) (p : B ⟶ D) (i : C ⟶ D)
    [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion i] [QuasiCompact k] [QuasiCompact i]
    [IsProper r] [IsProper p] (h : k ≫ p = r ≫ i) :
    ProperOpenPush Λ r ⋙ ProperOpenShriek Λ i ⟶
      ProperOpenShriek Λ k ⋙ ProperOpenPush Λ p
